title: Call: KYEM Area 1 Manager — "Put It in WebEOC as Missions"

transcript.speaker: KYEM Area 1 Manager
transcript.text: It's Area 1. I'm in the truck heading your way and I'm standing up for you. Frankfort has your county on the board. But I can't push anything up the chain until I see it written down.

transcript.speaker: KYEM Area 1 Manager
transcript.text: So, every request goes into WebEOC as a mission request. Quantity and delivery point, every time. Generators: what kW size, and which building. A cell-on-wheels: which tower area you need it to cover. Debris crews: which routes, in what order. If it just says 'need generators,' it sits in the queue.

transcript.speaker: KYEM Area 1 Manager
transcript.text: State highway crews can start moving at first light, around 06:45. I need your priority routes before then, or they'll start on the state roads, and that may not be what you want.

transcript.speaker: KYEM Area 1 Manager
transcript.text: One more thing. Has your Judge/Executive declared a local emergency? I'm not telling him to. But when I'm asking for state resources, a signed declaration makes it a lot easier.

transcript.speaker: KYEM Area 1 Manager
transcript.text: Okay. Get those missions in tonight, even rough ones. I'll check WebEOC at 02:00 and call you back. If your system's down, call the duty line and read them to me.

transcript.speaker: Text — County Judge/Executive
transcript.text: Text, 01:12: Corwin's mayor says he's signing a city declaration tonight. Do I need to sign a county one now, or wait for the damage numbers? I've got Ashford's mayor asking the same thing. Tell me what to do and where I need to be.

transcript.speaker: Email — NWS Paducah Warning Coordination Meteorologist
transcript.text: Email to the Brennan EOC, 01:14. Subject: *** EXERCISE *** Storm survey request, Brennan County, 12/12. *** EXERCISE — NOT A REAL PRODUCT *** Our storm survey team (two meteorologists) leaves Paducah at 06:30 and should reach Corwin around 07:30. We request escorted access to Corwin Wax & Candle, Pine Hollow and the Clarks River bridge. Please also send your timed damage reports, the 911 CAD times, spotter Brennan-14's account and any time-stamped photos or video. A preliminary EF rating for the Corwin track would follow Saturday afternoon. Please confirm a meeting point and an escort contact. Warning Coordination Meteorologist, NWS Paducah, 270-555-0163. *** EXERCISE ***

instructorNote: This shifts the room into recovery work. The EM Director should file specific WebEOC mission requests: generators sized for Brennan County High School and the Public Safety Building, a cell-on-wheels for Corwin, and debris clearance for the emergency routes. The Director should also advise the Judge/Executive to declare a local emergency now, coordinated with Corwin and Ashford. Watch whether Field sets up a 07:30 Sheriff escort for the survey that keeps it clear of the candle plant search. Also watch whether the Warning Officer pulls together the warning log, siren records, NWSChat transcripts and spotter reports under BWN 8. The text (01:12) and email (01:14) arrive just after the call ends.
